pageCache.pageTitle: Benson C of E Primary School - Science Ambassadors Blog
pageCache.text:
Science Ambassadors Blog
Welcome to our Blog!
We are the science ambassadors and we're here to tell you about science in our school. We love science because it is interesting and it challenges our minds.
See below to find out more about science in our school, Science Monkey, Nature Park, competitions and challenges, and more.
🌿 Nature’s Hidden Patterns Photography Challenge 📷
Calling all explorers! Have you ever noticed the swirling spirals in a snail’s shell, or the symmetry of a butterfly’s wings? Patterns are everywhere in nature, and now’s your chance to capture them in a photograph!
Why Enter? Spotting patterns sharpens your observational skills, helping you see the world in new ways. Patterns connect to science, maths, and art (where nature’s designs inspire creativity). Whether it’s the veins in a leaf or ripples in water, your discoveries reveal the magic behind everyday nature.
🏆 The science ambassadors will choose some children to share their photographs in assembly on 13th June.
So, grab your camera, step outside, and start seeing the world through a new lens.
Happy photographing!
We are thrilled to introduce a new member of our school community: Science Monkey! The children in Ash are trialling taking turns bringing Science Monkey home to explore the exciting world of science. If Science Monkey proves to be a hit, we plan to expand the program across the school so that all children will have the chance to engage in exciting science activities with it at home.
Science Monkey comes with a special diary where you and your child can record all the fun activities they do together. When it’s your child’s turn to host Science Monkey, we’d love for you to think of some science-related activities they could try. Encourage your child to document these experiences in the diary—photos of Science Monkey in action are always welcome!
Of course, you’re not limited to science experiments at home. You could take Science Monkey on adventures, such as nature spotting at the beach, fossil hunting, on nature walks, to a science museum, or even take it to a stargazing event or you could curl up on the sofa and watch a documentary or read a science book.
We look forward to hearing all about the science fun!
Thank you to Finty for fantastic sewing repairs and for making Science Monkey's accessories!
Submit your photo by 6th June.
Science Monkey's adventures so far...
Trout in the Classroom Chalk Streams Workshop
We (year 4 and 5) are taking part in the Trout in the Classroom Project, Chiltern Society. The project helps us learn about brown trout and the chalk stream habitat that they live in. We received the alevins in term 3. We are feeding and monitoring them until they have grown big enough to be released into the wild.

pageCache.pageTitle: Benson C of E Primary School - Worship and Reflection In School
pageCache.text:
Worship and Reflection In School
Whole school worship takes place three times a week, with Father Patrick visiting on Wednesdays. The Worship Leaders gather classes together with a bell and lead the prayers and readings. Children's prayers and reflections from the School Prayer Book are read regularly. Worship centres around themes/stories often linking to the school vision and values. The significant Christian festivals mark the year and children are also introduced to a variety of religious/cultural celebrations. For Christmas, Easter and the end of the academic year, the school holds worship in Church. During the summer months, worship is sometimes held outside.
Worship is designed to be inclusive and inspirational, to draw all participants in. It can include: music, story, drama, film, stillness, prayer and objects.
Class worship is based on the practice of Stilling or Dwelling in the Word (Reflecting on a Biblical verse.)The latter often follows the story for the week. Children feedback that they value the opportunity to be still and quiet within the school day.
Reflection Opportunities in Class- children have access to prayer boxes, holding crosses, prayer dice and prayer boxes. These can be found within Reading Areas or Reflection Spaces.
Prayer Space is a popular way for people of all ages to reflect or pray about things they are thankful for or to share concerns. Practical activities offer ways to think more deeply about things we care about. At this uncertain time, where mental wellbeing is just as important as physical health, there are some activities below to help with this.
For Christian families, worshipping at home, there is a pack containing some useful ideas.
Reflections For Children and Families
As part of their learning about prayer, Ash Class panned a prayer space for the rest of the school. They planned opportunities to reflect upon worries, celebrate the world and to be still.

Safeguarding Children
Our governors and staff team are committed to safeguarding the children in our care. The school has clear procedures where a child is considered to be at risk of harm and reserves the right to share information with external agencies.
Our Safeguarding Lead is Mrs Amy Pearce
Deputy Safeguarding Leads: Mrs Maritza Agudelo, Mrs Louisa Fanstone and Mrs Sarah Launchbury-Rainey
These staff can all be contacted through by emailing office.3181@benson.oxon.sch.uk or phoning the school on 01491 202502
Safeguarding Governor: Mrs Sara Ogden
The school has a safeguarding email for urgent concerns that is monitored out of school hours:
safeguarding@benson.oxon.sch.uk
We have a number of policies and procedures in place that contribute to our safeguarding commitment. Please see the files here for more information.
Keeping Children Safe in Education 2025
Child Protection Safeguarding Policy PDF File
Early Help
Early help is the provision of support to a child, young person or their family when problems or challenges emerge, with the aim of preventing issues from escalating or worsening. For families accessing Early Help, the below leaflet provides further information about this.
Early Help Guide for Families PDF File
Safeguarding Curriculum
We teach children how to stay safe through our SCARF (Safety, Caring, Achievement, Resilience, Friendship) curriculum as well as utilising other specific support such as NSPCC workshops and online safety through our Computing curriculum.
For more information, please click on the document below.
​If you are concerned about the safety or well-being of a child please speak directly to one of the named designated members of staff. Parents/carers/members of the public can also contact the Multi Agency Safeguarding Hub (MASH) 0345 050 7666. The NSPCC website is recommended for information for parents/carers regarding keeping children safe.
Children can contact Childline 0800 1111 childline.org.uk
For an illustrated guide for children explaining how different people and organisations work together to help, support and protect them (working together to safeguard children), click here.
For information about Domestic Abuse Support Services, click here.
Safeguarding Curriculum PDF File
Prevent Extremism
The prevent strategy is part of the UK Counter Terorism Strategy (CONTEST) published by the Government in 2011.
Prevent has three main objectives to :
1. respond to the ideological challenge of terrorism
2. support vulnerable people and prevent people from being drawn into terrorism
3. work with key sectors and institutions and address risks
It focuses on early intervention before any illegal activity takes place. The aim is to reduce the likelihood of individuals who support a violent extremist ideology of becoming terrorists. Find out more about the Prevent Strategy below.

pageCache.text:
Benson Buddies Wrap Around Care
From September 2026, breakfast club and after school club will be run by the school for children in Reception to Year 6. We are currently unable to offer places for Nursery age children.
Breakfast club 7.30am - 8.45am £6.50
After School Club 3.15pm - 5.30pm £15.00
Please click here to book: Benson Buddies - session bookings – Fill in form
Initially all bookings will need to be a term in advance (short terms) and we will be unable to accept any last minute/ad-hoc bookings. We will review this as the club becomes more established. We are able to accept tax-free childcare vouchers.
To enable us to get the club up and running from September, we need to ask parents to block book. Once we are up and running and have a clearer understanding of numbers of children and staffing, we plan to be able to offer ad-hoc bookings, hopefully from after October half-term. We do appreciate this is inflexible, but it is essential initially for us to be able to run the club.
We appreciated JAG (previous Wrap Around Care provider) offered a 4.30pm pick up at a lower cost. This is not something financially we are able to offer currently, but we will review this once the after-school club is up and running.
We will be accepting tax-free childcare. We would appreciate it if you could pay for a term at a time but will review if we can offer monthly once the club us up and running.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
'The school sets high expectations for all pupils. From the early years onwards, pupils learn to read well and develop a secure understanding of mathematics. They make meaningful links between their learning and real-life experiences, such as connecting a visit to a local castle with their history work on the Tudors. Pupils talk with increasing confidence about their work in school. The curriculum is well sequenced and builds from the early years onwards. As a result, pupils are increasingly able to make connections in their learning and build on what they already know.' Ofsted July 2025
